---
applyTo: "src/apps/pinch/**"
---

# Pinch rules

Applies on top of CLAUDE.md to everything under `src/apps/pinch/`. Keep the other copy of this file identical in body.

- **Theme: a warm kitchen, quietly.** Surfaces are paper-warm (cream by day, warm black by night) with hairline borders, and a soft shadow only where something floats (the nav pill, a popover, a sheet). Buttons are espresso-ink filled (`--color-primary`) for the one action on a screen and see-through with a hairline for the rest; never a block of orange. Warmth comes from peach tints (`bg-accent`, `--pinch-drizzle-soft`) on groups, fact chips, selected pills and the cards that need a nudge of attention, and from orange as the accent: the today dot (`--pinch-drizzle-fill` with `--pinch-drizzle-fill-foreground`, the only place text sits on the orange), a selected outline and ring, the active tab icon, the default product's star, the dashed "New" pills. A screen still reads clean: tint a few things, not everything. The palette, radii, hairlines and field inset live in `pinch.css` as tokens on `html.pinch-theme`, switched on by `usePinchTheme()` while the app is mounted so portaled modals and drawers match. Change the look there, not per component, use semantic tokens (`bg-primary`, `bg-accent`) and the drizzle variable (`text-[var(--pinch-drizzle)]`) rather than raw colors, and body and row text stays the normal color (the tertiary-button rule in `pinch.css`). The app icon and banner follow the other apps: a black tile or banner, the white mark and name, and "Moondreams Dev" in grey.
- **Shape language.** Corners are set by the raised `--radius-*` tokens, so don't hand-roll radii. Options a person picks among are `Pill`s, never radios or a tab strip; an option is a hairline pill and the selected one gets a drizzle outline so its emoji stays readable. Navigation is a floating pill at the bottom of a phone, as wide as its three tabs and never stretched across the screen (Calendar, Recipes, Kitchen: `PinchNav`), and the same tabs stand in a rail on the left edge from `lg` up. Later Kitchen entries join the Kitchen tab and never add a fourth.
- **Wide screens use the width, not a stretched phone.** The calendar's cells show meal emoji chips on a soft tint of the meal's colour below `lg` and, from `lg`, Google-Calendar-style pills with the meal's truncated title; Week is an agenda on a phone and seven columns from `lg`; Recipes and Kitchen run in two columns from `lg`. The phone layout is unchanged. Check a new screen at 1280px as well as 390px.
- **The calendar is Month, Week and Day, with a Today button.** The switch is a thin `PillGroup` in `PeriodSwitcher`, the arrows step by the view's unit, Today appears only while today is outside the shown period, and the stats and tiles always describe the shown period. A view that reaches past the loaded month window moves the listener's window; paging inside it never does.
- **Emoji carry meaning.** Meals are 🍳 breakfast, 🥪 lunch, 🍝 dinner, 🍿 snack, 🍰 dessert, 🥤 drink, in that order; the same six colors are the `--pinch-meal-*` tokens (and their `-soft` tints behind the calendar's chips and pills). Calories and macros are 🔥 calories (whole numbers), 💪 protein, 🌾 carbs and 🥑 fat in grams, everywhere they appear, through the shared `MacroStats` and its one emoji map `MACRO_EMOJIS` (inline in a row, tiles in a summary, `isCompact` tiles where space is tight), never a sentence of figures. A recipe's facts (🍽️ servings, 🔪 prep, ⏲️ cook) are one plain line of emoji and text, never pills. Ingredients have no icon for now (the approach is being rethought), so a row is its name; never a sparkle for "other".
- **Missing details appear only as in-context nudge lines.** A missing price, package size or nutrition value is one quiet line where it changes a number ("2 ingredients need a price · Add prices"), with a close button and a short fill-in sheet. Never a to-do list, a badge, a required field or a setup step, and a total says what it leaves out through a warning icon beside it (`HelpTip variant='warning'`) that opens like the help icon ("This leaves out 2 ingredients because there's no price for them yet"), and the fix stays one tap away on the drawers.
- **Three layers, recipes name only the ingredient.** Family, ingredient, product. A recipe or meal refers to an ingredient id, never a store or product; prices live on products.
- **The nudge lives on the drawers, not in the plate builder.** The recipe, saved meal, day and planned meal views carry "Add prices" (closing the drawer before the fill-in sheet opens); the meal builder is a full-screen subview, so it shows "Cost $0.08" with the warning icon, which opens its small help modal on a phone (the one overlay allowed over a subview) and a tooltip on a computer, and nothing else opens over it. A frozen day has no nudge, since a new price can't change it, and its warning, tile and rows say so ("This day has passed, so a price you add now counts from today on", "Fixed when the day passed", "Wasn't priced").
- **"Yours" is what you added, adjusted, priced or cook with.** Custom ingredients, adjusted catalog ones, ones with a product and ones a recipe, a saved meal or a planned day that isn't frozen yet uses; typing in the search looks through every ingredient, so a first-run kitchen never hears "nothing matches" for something the catalog has. Removing an in-use recipe, ingredient or store says it is taken off your lists, not erased, and a store the person adds back from the list comes back. The "Needs a price" and "Has a price" filters only look through Yours, and the filter panel says so, so a count of "22 ingredients" never reads as the whole catalog.
- **A new recipe asks how to start, with every way side by side, and each way is its own view.** A drawer on a phone, the page's own list from `sm` up (`MethodPicker`, rows only): From text, From a file ("A photo, screenshot or PDF"), From a link, then "Write it yourself" last and quieter. Picking one only picks: the text box, the file drop or the link field lives on its own screen (back raises the phone's drawer again, or returns to the list from `sm` up, and each says "Write it yourself instead"), never revealed under the list; the button reads "Fill in the recipe", and leaving a form that holds typed or read-in work asks Keep editing / Discard. The readings fill the real form for review and never save. Everything a recipe normally has (servings, times, photo, description, where it's from, ingredients, steps, nutrition) is a visible section of the form, never a "+ Add X" chip. Nutrition shows what was calculated per serving, lets the person change any number and reset to the calculated ones; a number equal to the calculated one stays derived.
- **The recipe form's editors are the drawers allowed over a subview.** The form's basics are summary rows, not boxes: Title, Prep and cook and Description each show a small caption, the value (the description clamped to two lines) and a chevron, and open their editor (`SummaryEditor`: a drawer on a phone or a short screen, a popover under the row from `sm`, each ending in Done; Enter in a one-line field closes it and never saves the recipe, and Escape or the back gesture closes only the editor). Servings stays an inline stepper. A recipe written from scratch opens its title editor once by itself; one from a reading, and any existing recipe, opens with every row closed. A bad value (minutes that aren't whole, a text over its limit) shows in red on its row as well as in the editor, and the pinned footer says what to fix. Prep and cook are two number fields, "Prep time" and "Cook time", each with a visible "min" suffix, never "(minutes)" in a label. On a phone adding and editing an ingredient (search, then amount, unit and note), a step (one text box) or the nutrition numbers (four small fields and "Reset to what we calculated") each happens in a drawer on top of the recipe form, ending in Done (and "Add another" while adding); a drawer holds one level, never opens another overlay, and from `sm` up a row opens in place. A screen's header carries the recipe's or meal's name as it is typed.
- **Taking a row out of a form is undoable for a few seconds.** Removing an ingredient or step from the recipe form (the ✕, the trash, or "Remove" in a drawer) or an item from the meal builder's plate takes it out at once and floats "Removed Salt · Undo · 6" above the pinned footer (`UndoSnackbar` over `useUndoRemoval`, counting 6 to 1): Undo puts the row back where it was, one removal is pending at a time (a newer one makes the older final), and the removal stands when the count ends. Whole-record deletes (a recipe, meal, ingredient, store, product) keep their confirm dialogs.
- **Nutrition is entered on the label's basis and stored per 100 g.** The ingredient form asks "Per [amount] [g | oz | serving]" above the four numbers, converts to `nutritionPer100g`, shows what it saved ("Saved as per 100 g: 🔥200") and refuses a blank or absurd number with one line. The serving option waits for a serving size that converts to grams. The ingredient drawer switches between per serving and per 100 g and hides the switch when both would show the same numbers.
- **Rows can hide their numbers, and start with the fewest.** Kitchen and Recipes/Meals have one View options control (an eye button, `ListViewControls` over the shared `ViewOptions`): show prices, show calories and macros, and the nutrition basis, remembered on the device per person. A list starts with prices on and calories and macros off (the eye button turns them on, and a choice already stored is kept); the macros switch is also off and disabled, with a line saying why, while no metric is on in Settings. Prices and macros are independent lines on a row, hiding one never changes a total, and the ingredient drawer's per serving / per 100 g switch is the same setting as the list's, so a row and its drawer never disagree. A row is as tall as its lines: a title-only ingredient row is about 44px, one with a price line about 60px, and a row with a leading tile or logo is as tall as the tile; never a `min-h` that leaves blank space under a lone title. `FamilyGroup` and the recipe list estimate their height from the lines that will show (price and nutrition), so the scrollbar doesn't jump when an option changes.
- **Every recipe reading discloses first.** The photo, text and link ways each open their own line ("An AI reads the picture and fills in the form. It isn't saved.") before anything is sent; a row the reader couldn't match keeps its amount, says "Not in your ingredients yet · tap to add or choose", and the footer says why Add is disabled.
- **A details drawer keeps its actions together.** The footer is Modify (secondary, left) beside the one primary (Add to calendar, Plan it) which takes the leftover width; the front matter is one plain emoji line (servings, prep, cook) and tiles (a Cost tile with its warning icon, emoji macro tiles), never pills or grey sentences; the ingredient drawer's line gives every fact an emoji (✏️ for yours, 🍽️ for the serving) and the family name its weight.
- **Where a recipe came from is a `Source`, never `Recipe.source`.** A source is an id and a label (`sources`, named by `Recipe.sourceId`); `source` only says how a draft was made. Readers go through `getRecipeSource`, so a missing key, `null` and a deleted source all mean "no source", and deleting a source clears `sourceId` on its recipes in batches without touching their `updatedAt` (it versions the cover) and never deletes a recipe. The recipe form's optional "Where it's from" is a visible `PickOrCreate` after the description that reuses a label already there (ignoring case) and, for a recipe read from a link, starts on the site without taking focus. The Sources entry (Kitchen's `EntryRow`) and the Recipes filter (a `FilterBar` with one Source question, pills with counts, "No source · n" only when some recipe has none) appear only once there is something to list, and a failed sources listener never reaches the load-error screen.
- **The shopping list is one line per ingredient and unit, filled from a sheet that picks what goes on it.** An item is `shoppingItems/{ingredientId}__{unit}`, so adding the same thing again merges: an unchecked line gains the amount (two decimals), a checked one starts again unchecked, a missing one is created, all in one `runTransaction` that reads every target first; units are never converted. Lines come from the pure `utils/shopping.ts` (a recipe scaled by servings over its own; a meal, planned meal or day: recipe items by their servings, ingredient items at their serving size) and are checked by `npm run check:pinch-math`. Ticking, changing and removing are field-scoped writes that touch only their own row (no sheet-wide busy), "Clear" is a chunked batch delete, and the 200 lines per add and the 300-item soft cap are the app's limits, not the rules'. The recipe, saved meal, planned meal and day drawers each carry a tinted "Add to shopping list" row in the body (not on a day that has passed) that closes the drawer and opens `AddToShoppingSheet`: a recipe gets a servings stepper, every line starts ticked except one already on the list ("On your list · 2 lb"), one scrolling list sits under a fixed header, and a toast says what was added with a "View" button. The list is Kitchen's full-width `EntryRow` with the count left to buy and a `Subview` grouped by family (the first three groups draw at once, the rest near the viewport, a group draws 100 rows then "Show N more"), with "Got it" collapsed beside its "Clear"; its row and add sheets open over it like Stores' and Sources'. Its cost line says "About" (the amounts priced from default products, not packages) and names what it leaves out through the warning icon, and a failed shopping listener logs, clears its items and degrades only its own screen.
- **Vendored assets keep their licence.** Pinch vendors nothing right now (the ingredient icons were removed); a store logo comes from Logo.dev and is credited in Settings' About row. Add any new vendored set with its notice beside it.
- **Check lists at scale.** Pinch needs an oversized seed fixture like Waypoint's (`scripts/seeds/pinchScale.ts`, "Big Kitchen (scale test)"). Open new lists on it at phone width with the dev build throttled, and keep per-row work cheap (CLAUDE.md "Performance is a design check"): catalog groups mount only near the viewport (`LazyMount` plus `defer-offscreen`), and a long list (Products, a week's agenda) caps its rows with "Show N more".
